intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering.

experiences.name: Luau at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and haupia dessert. This award-winning luau is set on the oceanfront and provides a memorable cultural evening for all ages with storytelling that traces the history of Hawaii.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Nature Walk and Waterfall Swim
experiences.description: Hike through a lush botanical garden along a well-maintained family-friendly trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids and adults alike will love swimming in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall. The valley also features cultural demonstrations, wildlife, and ancient Hawaiian archaeological sites along the way.

experiences.name: Sunset Catamaran Sail along the Napali Coast
experiences.description: Embark on a breathtaking family catamaran cruise along Kauai's dramatic Napali Coast, featuring towering sea cliffs, hidden sea caves, and abundant marine life including spinner dolphins and humpback whales in season. The sunset timing creates a magical golden-hour backdrop over the cliffs, and light snacks and drinks are typically included in the tour price.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa
experiences.description: Spend a fun-filled afternoon exploring the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore, sampling world-famous shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and local Hawaiian plate lunches. This self-guided food adventure lets families stroll through boutique shops, art galleries, and soak in the laid-back surf culture that defines Hawaii's North Shore.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — skip morning activities. After landing, collect luggage, pick up a rental car or catch TheBus (Route 23) toward East Oahu, and check in to your Hanauma Bay boutique stay. Freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short walk to Hanauma Bay Overlook (free, no entry needed) for stunning panoramic views of the bay and coastline. Pick up a shave ice or snack from a nearby food truck to celebrate your arrival. Explore the immediate neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koko Marina Center (10 minutes away) for a relaxed first dinner. Stroll the marina area and watch the sunset over the water. Stop at a grocery store (Times Supermarket or Foodland) to stock up on breakfast supplies for the week — a huge budget saver.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport — skip to save money
meals.lunch: L&L Hawaiian Barbecue near the airport or a plate lunch from a local deli (~$10–13)
meals.dinner: Koko Marina Sushi or Zippy's at Koko Marina (~$12–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Rest is important after a long flight. Buy reusable water bottles and sunscreen at the grocery store tonight — both are expensive at tourist shops. Budget tip: stock your room with breakfast foods (yogurt, fruit, granola bars) to save $10–15/day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve (arrive by 7:00–7:30 AM to beat crowds and secure entry). Entry fee is $25/adult, free for Hawaii residents and children under 13. Watch the mandatory 9-minute reef education video, then snorkel the stunning bay — one of Hawaii's best snorkeling spots. Rental gear is available on-site (~$12–15).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the bay, drive or bus to Sandy Beach Park (5 minutes away) — completely free. Watch the famous bodysurfers tackle the powerful shore break (swimming here is expert-only, but watching is thrilling). Relax on the wide sandy beach and enjoy a packed lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Drive the scenic Makapuu Point area and stop at the Makapuu Lighthouse Trail trailhead to plan tomorrow's hike. Return to the hotel. Cook a simple dinner in your room or grab takeout.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — fruit, granola, yogurt from grocery store (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel room — sandwiches, chips, fruit (~$4–5)
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood (famous poke spot in Kaimuki, ~20 min drive) or takeout poke bowl (~$14–18)

day_by_day.notes: Book Hanauma Bay entry in advance online at hanauma bay.hawaii.gov — slots fill up fast, especially in summer. Arrive early to maximize time before the midday crowds. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreen is banned in the bay.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Makapuu Point Lighthouse Trail (free, paved, 2 miles round trip, moderate). Stunning coastal views, possible whale sightings in season, and views of Rabbit Island. Great for families with kids. Start by 8:00 AM before the heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Waimanalo Beach — consistently ranked one of Hawaii's most beautiful beaches (free parking). Swim, build sandcastles, and enjoy the calm, clear water. This is a local favorite, less touristy than Waikiki. Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kailua Town (~15 minutes from Waimanalo). Browse the boutique shops on Kailua Road (window shopping is free!). Grab an affordable dinner at one of the casual restaurants on the main strip.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Waimanalo Beach — deli sandwiches, chips, drinks packed from home (~$5–6)
meals.dinner: Kalapawai Cafe & Deli in Kailua — casual, affordable sandwiches and plates (~$13–17)

day_by_day.notes: Waimanalo Beach has free restrooms and showers. The drive along Kalanianaole Highway from Hanauma Bay to Waimanalo is scenic — take it slow. Kailua is a great town for families — very safe and walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Kailua Beach Park (free, 15 minutes from hotel). One of the top-rated beaches in the US — calm, turquoise water perfect for families. Rent a kayak or stand-up paddleboard from a local rental shop (~$25–35/hour for a double kayak) and paddle out to the Mokulua Islands (the 'Mokes') — a stunning, unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return kayaks and relax on Kailua Beach. Walk the length of the beach, collect shells, and let the kids play in the gentle surf. Visit the nearby Kalapawai Market for cold drinks and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward East Oahu. Stop at the Blowhole Lookout (Halona Blowhole) on the way home — free and dramatic ocean feature. Watch the ocean spray through the lava rock. Return to hotel for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market deli sandwiches and snacks eaten at the beach (~$10–14)
meals.dinner: Cook at the hotel or pick up a rotisserie chicken and sides from Foodland (~$12–15 for the family)

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rental tip: book through Twogood Kayaks or Kailua Beach Adventures for competitive rates. The paddle to the Mokes takes about 30–45 minutes each way — plan accordingly. The Halona Blowhole is best viewed when surf is moderate to high.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Diamond Head State Monument (~25 minutes from hotel). Hike the iconic Diamond Head Crater Trail (1.6 miles round trip, $5/person entry, or $10/vehicle). Stunning 360-degree views of Honolulu and the Pacific. Start early (gates open at 6:00 AM) to avoid heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through Waikiki Beach (free to walk and swim — the beach is public). Let the kids experience the famous surf and the lively atmosphere. Walk the beachfront promenade and watch the surfers. Visit the Duke Kahanamoku Statue for a photo op.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Waikiki's Kalakaua Avenue for window shopping. Grab affordable dinner at a local spot away from the hotel-row restaurants. Head back to East Oahu.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Waikiki — Rainbow Drive-In (local institution, plate lunches ~$10–13)
meals.dinner: Marugame Udon in Waikiki — fresh udon noodles, very affordable (~$8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head parking fills up fast — arrive before 8:00 AM or use TheBus from Waikiki (Route 23). Rainbow Drive-In is a must-try local spot that has been serving plate lunches since 1961. Waikiki beach is free — never pay for beach access.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum in Honolulu (~30 minutes from hotel) — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Entry is ~$25/adult, ~$17/children (ages 4–17). Spend 2–3 hours exploring Hawaiian history, artifacts, planetarium shows, and the Science Adventure Center (kids love it).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Chinatown Honolulu for a cultural afternoon. Walk the colorful streets, visit the Oahu Market, browse art galleries (many are free), and soak in the local atmosphere. The Foster Botanical Garden is nearby (free entry on certain days, otherwise $5/adult).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a budget-friendly dinner in Chinatown — some of the cheapest and most authentic food in Honolulu. Return to East Oahu for the evening.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Chinatown — Little Village Noodle House or a noodle shop (~$10–13 per person)
meals.dinner: Fook Yuen Restaurant or another Chinatown spot — large portions, very affordable (~$10–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bishop Museum tip: check their website for any free or discounted admission days. Chinatown is very walkable — park once and explore on foot. The Honolulu Farmers Market at Bishop Museum is held on Wednesdays but worth planning around on future trips.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the KCC Farmers Market at Kapiolani Community College (7:30 AM – 11:00 AM, free entry). One of the best farmers markets in Hawaii — sample local fruits, fresh malasadas, acai bowls, and Hawaiian specialties. Stock up on fresh produce and local snacks for the week. Very family-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Kapiolani Park (free) — Hawaii's oldest public park, right next to Waikiki. Fly kites, have a picnic, visit the Honolulu Zoo (entry ~$19/adult, ~$11/child — good value for families) or the free Waikiki Aquarium (~$12/adult, ~$5/child).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the free hula show at Kuhio Beach in Waikiki (held Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday evenings at 6:30 PM — free). A magical cultural experience for the whole family. Grab shave ice nearby for dessert.

meals.breakfast: KCC Farmers Market — fresh fruit, malasadas, acai bowl (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Kapiolani Park with farmers market finds (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Plate lunch from a food truck near Kapiolani Park or Waikiki (~$10–13)

day_by_day.notes: The KCC Farmers Market is very popular on Saturdays — arrive early for the best selection and shortest lines. The free hula show at Kuhio Beach is a highlight of any Oahu trip — bring a blanket to sit on. Check exact show times at the Waikiki Beach Special Events website.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore (~45–55 minutes from East Oahu). Stop at Haleiwa Town first — a charming surf town with free beaches, local shops, and the famous Matsumoto Shave Ice (~$4–6). Walk the main street and soak in the laid-back North Shore vibe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park (free) — a stunning, dramatic bay with a famous jump rock (seasonal, safe in summer when surf is calm). Swim, snorkel, or just relax on the beautiful beach. Continue to Sunset Beach for a walk and photos.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku on the way back — a North Shore institution. Famous garlic shrimp plates (~$14–16) served from a graffiti-covered truck. Return to East Oahu.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Matsumoto Shave Ice + a plate lunch from a North Shore food truck (~$12–15)
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck, Kahuku (~$14–16 per plate, shareable)

day_by_day.notes: North Shore traffic on weekends can be heavy — leave by 8:00 AM to beat it. In summer (August), the North Shore has very calm water — ideal for swimming and snorkeling. In winter, waves can be 20–30 feet — not swimmable but spectacular to watch. Waimea Bay jump rock is a beloved local tradition — kids love it!

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial (~35 minutes from hotel). The USS Arizona Memorial is free (boat tour tickets are timed-entry, free but must be reserved in advance at recreation.gov). Plan 3–4 hours for the full experience. A deeply moving and educational experience for older kids and adults.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, visit the Battleship Missouri Memorial (separate ticket ~$32/adult, ~$16/child) or the Pacific Aviation Museum (~$25/adult, ~$15/child) if budget allows — both are on Ford Island and highly rated. Alternatively, skip the paid attractions and return via the Pali Lookout (free) — dramatic views of the Windward Coast from the Ko'olau Mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final full evening. Return to Hanauma Bay area. Enjoy a sunset walk at your local beach. Treat the family to a nicer sit-down dinner to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor Café or packed lunch (~$10–13)
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner — Kona Brewing Company at Koko Marina (~$18–25 per person, great burgers and local beer)

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor USS Arizona Memorial boat tickets are FREE but must be reserved well in advance — book at recreation.gov as soon as possible. Arrive 30 minutes before your reservation. The experience is appropriate for children 4 and up, though the subject matter is sobering. The Pali Lookout is free and one of the most dramatic viewpoints on Oahu — do not skip it.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise swim at Hanauma Bay overlook or a nearby beach. Pack up your bags and do a final room check. Return any rental equipment. Take a slow, scenic drive along Kalanianaole Highway for final coastal views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time (allow 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights). Return rental car if applicable. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the airport — or better yet, pick up local items at grocery stores (Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, Hawaiian sea salt) which are far cheaper than airport gift shops.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with wonderful memories! (Schedule departure activities based on your actual flight time.)

meals.breakfast: Final in-room breakfast — use up remaining groceries (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Airport — Makai Market Food Court in Terminal 2 has affordable local options (~$12–15)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your layover destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget souvenir tip: Costco (if you have a membership), Times Supermarket, or Don Quijote store offer Kona coffee, chocolate-covered macadamia nuts, and Hawaiian-themed items at 30–50% less than airport or Waikiki shops. Pack reef-safe sunscreen and any opened food items in checked luggage. Leave no trace — Hawaii's ecosystems are fragile and beautiful.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay (approximately 30–45 min from HNL airport).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the scenic coastal path near Hanauma Bay to get your bearings. Enjoy the ocean views and let the kids stretch their legs after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Koko Marina Center or Hawaii Kai Town Center for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the waterfront area and watch the sunset over Maunalua Bay.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up poke bowls or plate lunches from Foodland Farms in Hawaii Kai — a great first taste of local Hawaiian food at an affordable price.
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company at Koko Marina — casual waterfront dining with fresh fish tacos, burgers, and craft beers. Family-friendly and mid-range priced.

day_by_day.notes: Reserve your Hanauma Bay snorkeling time slot online tonight for Day 2 — entry is limited and slots fill up fast. Tickets must be booked in advance at the official Hanauma Bay website.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles. Arrive early (pre-booked slot) to beat the crowds. Watch the mandatory marine education video before entering the water. Snorkel gear rentals available on-site.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive 10 minutes to Sandy Beach Park — one of Oahu's most dramatic shoreline spots. Watch experienced bodyboarders ride the powerful shorebreak (swimming here is for strong swimmers only; kids can play safely at the water's edge and explore tide pools).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay to rinse off and relax. Head to Hawaii Kai for dinner and a gentle evening walk along the marina.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the boutique stay or grab pastries and coffee from a nearby café before heading to Hanauma Bay.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or purchase snacks from the Hanauma Bay concession stand (sandwiches, fruit, shave ice). No outside food allowed inside the reserve, so eat at the designated picnic area.
meals.dinner: Plumeria Beach House at Hawaii Kai area or try Nico's at Pier 38 for fresh locally-caught fish plates. Mid-range, family-friendly atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned at Hanauma Bay to protect the coral. Bring water shoes for easier reef navigation. Parking at Hanauma Bay is limited; arrive by your reserved time.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail (20 min from hotel) — a paved, family-friendly 2-mile round-trip hike with stunning panoramic views of the windward coast, offshore islands, and (in season) humpback whales. Strollers are manageable on the paved path.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the windward coast to Waimanalo Beach — one of Oahu's longest and most beautiful white-sand beaches. Spend the afternoon swimming in calm, family-friendly turquoise waters. The beach is rarely overcrowded and perfect for building sandcastles.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Hawaii Kai and stop at a local farmers' market or shave ice stand in the area. Enjoy a relaxed evening dinner near the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast at the boutique stay or stop at a local diner such as Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen in Kailua for their famous macadamia nut pancakes (a short detour worth it).
meals.lunch: Pickup plate lunches from Keneke's BBQ in Waimanalo — a beloved local spot with kalua pork, loco moco, and fresh fish at very affordable prices.
meals.dinner: Assaggio Italian Restaurant in Hawaii Kai — family-friendly Italian with pasta, pizza, and seafood in a comfortable mid-range setting.

day_by_day.notes: The Makapu'u trail is exposed with little shade — bring hats, sunscreen, and plenty of water. Best done in the morning before peak heat. Waimanalo Beach has restroom facilities and lifeguards on duty.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Oahu's North Shore — drive approximately 1 hour from Hanauma Bay. Visit Waimea Valley for the Waimea Valley Nature Walk and Waterfall Swim. Hike through a lush botanical garden along a well-maintained family-friendly trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids can swim in the freshwater pool at the base of the waterfall (life jackets provided).
day_by_day.afternoon: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa — Spend a fun-filled afternoon exploring the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore. Sample world-famous shave ice at Matsumoto's or Aoki's, browse local boutiques, and soak in the laid-back surf culture. Walk the historic town center and stop at local food trucks for snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Sunset Beach or Ehukai Beach Park before the drive back to Hanauma Bay. The North Shore evening light is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast burritos or açaí bowls from a food truck near Haleiwa on the way up, or eat at the boutique stay before departing.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — the iconic North Shore garlic shrimp plate truck is a must-try Hawaiian experience. Affordable and delicious.
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Joe's Seafood Grill — a beloved North Shore institution with fresh seafood, tropical cocktails, and ocean views. Mid-range pricing. Head back to hotel after dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Valley charges an entry fee (~$20 adults, ~$10 children). Book tickets online in advance. The waterfall swim area requires life jackets (provided free). North Shore surf can be very large in winter but August is typically calmer and safer for families.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Diamond Head State Monument — a short 20-minute drive from the hotel. Hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit of this famous volcanic crater for breathtaking 360-degree views of Honolulu, Waikiki, and the Pacific Ocean. The trail involves some stairs and a tunnel but is manageable for families with older children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for a classic Hawaiian beach afternoon. Rent bodyboards or try a beginner surf lesson at one of the many surf schools along the beach. The gentle waves at Waikiki are perfect for first-timers and kids.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue in Waikiki for shopping and people-watching. Visit the International Market Place for dinner and entertainment in an open-air setting.

meals.breakfast: Grab acai bowls or smoothies from Bogart's Café near Diamond Head — a local favorite with fresh, healthy options.
meals.lunch: Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant with burgers, fish tacos, and tropical drinks. Named after legendary surfer Duke Kahanamoku. Mid-range pricing.
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — an extremely popular and affordable Japanese udon restaurant with fresh hand-pulled noodles. Expect a short line but very fast service and great value.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires advance reservations and a parking reservation or use TheBus/rideshare. The hike is best done in the morning before heat builds. Bring water and wear sturdy footwear. Surf lessons in Waikiki typically run $35–$55 per person for group lessons.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center (PCC) in Laie on the windward coast — a world-class family attraction featuring six authentic Pacific Island village experiences (Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, Aotearoa). Spend the morning exploring the villages, watching cultural demonstrations, and participating in hands-on activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Polynesian Cultural Center — watch the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show (pre-book tickets). Alternatively, enjoy the canoe pageant on the lagoon in the afternoon, which is a highlight for families.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show at PCC — a stunning theatrical production telling the story of a Polynesian family across generations, featuring fire knife dancing, acrobatics, and traditional music. Combine with an Ali'i Luau buffet dinner package.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or grab something quick before the drive to Laie (approximately 45 minutes from Hanauma Bay).
meals.lunch: Dining at the Polynesian Cultural Center's Gateway Restaurant — buffet-style with Hawaiian and Pacific Island dishes included in many ticket packages.
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau dinner buffet at PCC — included with evening show packages. Features traditional Hawaiian foods including kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia (coconut pudding).

day_by_day.notes: Book PCC tickets well in advance online — combo packages (villages + luau + show) offer the best value at approximately $120–$160 per adult, $80–$110 per child. Allow a full day for this experience. PCC is operated by Brigham Young University Hawaii and alcohol is not served on premises.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the boutique stay — sleep in, enjoy breakfast, and spend time at the hotel pool or take a morning walk along the coastal trail near Hanauma Bay. This is a designated rest and recovery morning after the full day at PCC.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Sea Life Park Hawaii in Waimanalo (15 minutes from hotel) — a family-friendly marine park featuring dolphin encounters, penguin exhibits, sea turtle lagoon, and Hawaiian monk seal presentations. Kids can interact with stingrays and enjoy live animal shows.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from Alan Davis Beach (near Makapu'u) or the scenic lookout near the hotel. Enjoy a low-key evening close to the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay or nearby café. Try Kaimana Beach Hotel's Hau Tree Restaurant for a special brunch experience.
meals.lunch: Grab food at Sea Life Park's on-site café or pack lunch from a nearby grocery store for a picnic at the park.
meals.dinner: Roy's Restaurant in Hawaii Kai — a celebrated Hawaiian fusion restaurant by Chef Roy Yamaguchi. Slightly upscale but excellent value for a special family dinner. Signature dishes include misoyaki butterfish and molten chocolate soufflé.

day_by_day.notes: Sea Life Park admission is approximately $40–$50 per adult and $25–$35 per child. Dolphin swim encounters are an additional cost (~$150–$200 per person) and must be booked in advance. Check the show schedule upon arrival to plan your visit around live presentations.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum in Honolulu (30 minutes from hotel) — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore the Hawaiian Hall, Pacific Hall, and the Science Adventure Center. The planetarium shows are a highlight for kids. Learn about Hawaii's volcanic origins, ancient Polynesian navigation, and royal Hawaiian history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore historic downtown Honolulu — visit Iolani Palace (the only royal palace on U.S. soil), the Kamehameha Statue, and Kawaiahao Church. Walk through the historic district and browse the Chinatown neighborhood for local art galleries and unique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Honolulu's vibrant restaurant scene in Chinatown or the Kakaako neighborhood — one of Oahu's trendiest dining districts with street art murals, craft breweries, and diverse restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Leonard's Bakery in Honolulu — famous for malasadas (Portuguese doughnuts), a beloved Hawaii tradition. A must-visit stop on the way to the Bishop Museum.
meals.lunch: Livestock Tavern in Chinatown — farm-to-table American bistro with excellent burgers, fresh salads, and local ingredients. Mid-range pricing.
meals.dinner: Kakaako Kitchen — casual, locally-sourced Hawaiian comfort food in the Kakaako neighborhood. Known for fresh fish plates, sandwiches, and local-style sides at very reasonable prices.

day_by_day.notes: Bishop Museum is open Tuesday–Sunday; verify hours in advance. Iolani Palace requires a timed entry tour reservation — book online ahead of time. Parking in downtown Honolulu can be challenging; consider using a rideshare service for this day.

day_by_day.morning: Kailua Beach day — drive 30 minutes to the windward side to visit Kailua Beach, consistently rated one of America's best beaches. The calm, crystal-clear turquoise waters and powdery white sand make it ideal for families. Rent kayaks or stand-up paddleboards from Kailua Beach Adventures to paddle out to the Mokulua Islands offshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kailua Town — browse the charming boutique shops, art galleries, and local stores along Kailua Road. Visit Lanikai Beach (a short walk or drive from Kailua Beach) for more stunning scenery and calm swimming conditions. The Lanikai Pillbox hike offers spectacular ridge views (moderate difficulty, 1.8 miles round-trip).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Hanauma Bay area for a final relaxed evening. Consider a sunset dinner cruise or simply watch the sunset from a scenic lookout near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — a beloved local breakfast institution famous for red velvet pancakes, eggs benedict, and guava chiffon pancakes. Arrive early as lines form quickly.
meals.lunch: Island Snow in Kailua for shave ice (Barack Obama's favorite shave ice spot!) plus grab a poke bowl from Aloha Salads or a plate lunch from a local food truck.
meals.dinner: Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Lanikai — a Kailua institution since 1962 with fresh fish, steaks, and salad bar. Casual, family-friendly, and mid-range priced. Request a table with garden views.

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach parking fills up quickly on weekends — arrive by 9:00 AM. Kayak rentals to the Mokulua Islands run approximately $60–$80 for a double kayak. The Lanikai Pillbox hike is best done in the morning before heat builds; it involves some steep sections not suitable for very young children.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Hanauma Bay area — take one last walk along the coastal path, collect shells at a nearby beach, or revisit your favorite spot from the trip. Pack souvenirs and do any final shopping. Visit the nearby Koko Head Café for a special farewell breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: visit the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (open Wed, Sat, Sun) or the Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall — for last-minute souvenirs, macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and Hawaiian gifts. Ala Moana is 25 minutes from the hotel and close to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Honolulu International Airport (HNL) — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights. Enjoy one final plate lunch or shave ice at the airport's local food options before departure.

meals.breakfast: Koko Head Café in Kaimuki — a celebrated brunch spot known for creative Hawaiian-inspired egg dishes, kimchi fried rice, and loco moco. One of Oahu's most popular breakfast destinations for a memorable farewell meal.
meals.lunch: Poke bowl from Foodland Farms or Ono Seafood in Kaimuki — fresh, affordable, and quintessentially Hawaiian for a final taste of the islands.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner at a restaurant near Ala Moana Center such as Yardhouse or Mariposa at Neiman Marcus (splurge option) before heading to the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and arrange airport transportation in advance. Traffic on H-1 freeway toward the airport can be heavy during afternoon rush hour (3:00–6:00 PM) — plan accordingly. Check out of the boutique stay by the standard 11:00 AM checkout time and store luggage if needed for afternoon activities. Mahalo for a wonderful trip to Hawaii!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering.

experiences.name: Luau at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and haupia dessert. This award-winning luau is set on the oceanfront and provides a memorable cultural evening for all ages with storytelling that traces the history of Hawaii.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Nature Walk and Waterfall Swim
experiences.description: Hike through a lush botanical garden along a well-maintained family-friendly trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids and adults alike will love swimming in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall. The valley also features cultural demonstrations, wildlife, and ancient Hawaiian archaeological sites along the way.

experiences.name: Sunset Catamaran Sail along the Napali Coast
experiences.description: Embark on a breathtaking family catamaran cruise along Kauai's dramatic Napali Coast, featuring towering sea cliffs, hidden sea caves, and abundant marine life including spinner dolphins and humpback whales in season. The sunset timing creates a magical golden-hour backdrop over the cliffs, and light snacks and drinks are typically included in the tour price.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa
experiences.description: Spend a fun-filled afternoon exploring the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore, sampling world-famous shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and local Hawaiian plate lunches. This self-guided food adventure lets families stroll through boutique shops, art galleries, and soak in the laid-back surf culture that defines Hawaii's North Shore.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private check-in experience at the boutique property with welcome refreshments and a personalized orientation of the resort amenities. Settle into your suite, unpack, and take a leisurely stroll along the nearby shoreline to begin soaking in the island atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private lanai or the hotel's ocean-view terrace, followed by a welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant or a short drive to a top East Oahu dining destination.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy snacks or a meal on the flight before arrival.
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by the boutique hotel upon check-in — tropical fruit platters, local cheeses, and fresh juices.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Roy's Hawaii Kai (East Oahu) — celebrated Hawaiian Fusion cuisine with fresh catch, wagyu beef, and an extensive wine list in an elegant yet relaxed setting perfect for families.

day_by_day.notes: Request the hotel arrange a private luxury airport transfer in advance. Ask the concierge to pre-book all upcoming experiences this evening to secure prime time slots. Hydrate well and rest early to adjust to the time zone.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — just minutes from the hotel, this is Hawaii's premier marine sanctuary. Arrive early (reserve the first entry slot via the hotel concierge) to enjoy calm, uncrowded waters. A private guide will accompany the family to identify vibrant reef fish, sea turtles, and coral formations in the crystal-clear bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the boutique stay for a poolside lunch, then enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the hotel's private beach area. Optional: book a family stand-up paddleboard lesson on the calm waters near the property.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Koko Head coastal path, followed by a refined dinner at a nearby East Oahu restaurant.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast delivered by the hotel — fresh acai bowls, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, Kona coffee, and tropical juices.
meals.lunch: Poolside dining at the boutique hotel — gourmet sandwiches, poke bowls, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Koko Head Café (East Oahu) for an upscale brunch-dinner experience, or a private in-suite chef dinner arranged through the hotel concierge for a truly exclusive family evening.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations; the hotel concierge should secure these immediately upon check-in. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — it is required at the bay. Bring water shoes for the reef entry.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury vehicle day trip to Oahu's North Shore. Begin with the Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa — explore the charming surf town, sample legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, taste garlic shrimp from iconic food trucks, browse local boutiques, and experience the authentic laid-back North Shore culture with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the North Shore to watch world-class surfers at Sunset Beach or Banzai Pipeline (August swells are moderate — ideal for families to enjoy safely from the beach). Optional: a private surf lesson for older children at a calmer nearby break arranged through the tour operator.
day_by_day.evening: Scenic drive back to East Oahu along the windward coast (Pali Highway) with a stop at the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout for breathtaking panoramic views of the Ko'olau Mountains and windward coastline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Hawaiian pancakes with macadamia nut butter, fresh papaya, and Kona coffee before departing.
meals.lunch: Part of the Haleiwa food tour experience — gourmet shave ice, fresh poke, garlic shrimp plates, and local tropical fruit tastings.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vintage Cave Honolulu (Ala Moana area, 30-minute drive) — one of Hawaii's most exclusive fine dining experiences with a chef's tasting menu, exceptional wine pairings, and an intimate atmosphere. Advance reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 8:30 AM to make the most of the North Shore before crowds arrive. The hotel concierge should arrange a premium SUV with a private driver for the day. Vintage Cave requires reservations well in advance — book tonight if not already done.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (HNL) to Maui (OGG) on a short inter-island flight (approx. 30 minutes). Arrange a private luxury transfer to the Lahaina/Ka'anapali area on Maui's west coast. Check in at a premium Maui resort (e.g., Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea or Montage Kapalua Bay — pre-book before the trip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the Maui resort and spend the afternoon at the resort's private beach or pool. Enjoy complimentary snorkel gear, paddleboards, and beach amenities provided by the resort. The calm, warm waters of Ka'anapali or Wailea Beach are perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: Luau at Old Lahaina Luau — widely regarded as the most authentic and culturally rich luau in all of Hawaii. Enjoy traditional imu-roasted kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, hula performances, and fire dancing in an intimate oceanfront setting in historic Lahaina. A truly unforgettable family experience.

meals.breakfast: Quick early breakfast at the boutique hotel before transfer to the airport — yogurt parfaits, pastries, and fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the Maui resort's oceanfront restaurant — fresh grilled fish tacos, island salads, and tropical cocktails/mocktails.
meals.dinner: Full traditional Hawaiian feast included at the Old Lahaina Luau — kalua pig, lomi lomi salmon, poi, fresh fish, tropical desserts, and open bar with mai tais and non-alcoholic options.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Old Lahaina Luau as far in advance as possible — it sells out months ahead, especially in August. Arrange the inter-island flight and Maui resort in advance. The luau begins around sunset; arrive 30 minutes early for the best seating.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Road to Hana private driving tour with a local expert guide. Depart early to beat traffic along the iconic 64-mile coastal highway, stopping at Twin Falls, Wai'anapanapa Black Sand Beach, bamboo forests, and dramatic sea cliffs. The private guide ensures a comfortable, curated pace perfect for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hana Town for lunch. Explore the serene, remote eastern tip of Maui including the Seven Sacred Pools (Ohe'o Gulch) in Haleakala National Park, where families can wade in natural freshwater pools surrounded by lush rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey along the southern route (Piilani Highway) past Tedeschi Winery and upcountry Maui landscapes, arriving back at the resort in time for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early in-room breakfast at the Maui resort before departure — continental spread with fresh island fruit, pastries, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Hasegawa General Store picnic provisions in Hana, or a stop at Braddah Hutt for fresh banana bread, tropical smoothies, and local snacks along the road.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mama's Fish House (Paia, on the return route) — Hawaii's most iconic seafood restaurant with daily-caught fish named after the local fishermen who caught them. Romantic, family-friendly, and absolutely world-class. Reservations essential months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Depart no later than 6:30 AM to fully enjoy the Road to Hana. Wear comfortable shoes for short trail walks. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, insect repellent, and light rain jackets — the Hana coast receives frequent tropical showers. The private guide is strongly recommended over self-driving for families.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of Maui and the neighboring island of Molokai — experience the West Maui Mountains, Haleakala crater, remote sea cliffs, and hidden waterfalls from the air in a doors-off or luxury enclosed helicopter. A breathtaking, once-in-a-lifetime family experience lasting approximately 60–90 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a spa afternoon. Parents can enjoy treatments at the resort's luxury spa (couples massage, Hawaiian lomi lomi massage) while children enjoy supervised resort kids' club activities — snorkeling lessons, hula classes, or lei-making workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's oceanfront bar, then a leisurely private beach bonfire experience arranged by the concierge — complete with s'mores, Hawaiian music, and stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or à la carte at the resort's main restaurant — eggs any style, loco moco, fresh açaí bowls, and Maui-grown coffee.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — gourmet salads, fresh sashimi, lobster rolls, and fresh-pressed tropical juices.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite or beachside dinner prepared by a private chef arranged through the resort concierge — a customized multi-course Hawaiian menu with wine pairing, served under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour well in advance through Blue Hawaiian Helicopters or Maverick Helicopters — both offer premium family-friendly options. Confirm weight limits and age restrictions for children when booking. The private beach bonfire should be arranged through the concierge at least 24 hours ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Maui (OGG) to Kauai (LIH) on an inter-island flight. Private luxury transfer to a premium resort on Kauai's South Shore (e.g., Grand Hyatt Kauai Resort & Spa or Timbers Kauai — pre-book). Check in and explore the resort grounds, which typically feature spectacular lagoon pools, lazy rivers, and direct beach access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Waimea Valley Nature Walk and Waterfall Swim on Kauai's North Shore — a family-friendly guided hike through a lush botanical garden with over 5,000 tropical plant species, culminating in a swim at the stunning 45-foot Waihi Falls waterfall. The well-maintained trail is suitable for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the south shore resort for dinner and a relaxed evening enjoying the resort's evening entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the Maui resort before the airport transfer.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in Waimea Valley provided by the tour operator, or stop at a local Hanalei food truck for fresh fish plates and tropical smoothies on the North Shore.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Merriman's Fish House Kauai (Poipu) — farm-to-table Hawaiian regional cuisine with ocean views, featuring locally sourced ingredients, fresh Kauai fish, and an impressive wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Valley is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the South Shore resort — arrange a private driver for the day. Life jackets are provided at the waterfall swimming area. The trail is paved and stroller-accessible. Bring a change of clothes for after the waterfall swim.

day_by_day.morning: Sunset Catamaran Sail along the Napali Coast — embark on a premium morning catamaran cruise (departing from Port Allen Marina) along Kauai's dramatic and otherworldly Napali Coast. Marvel at 4,000-foot sea cliffs, hidden sea caves, cascading waterfalls, and pristine blue waters. Snorkel in protected coves and watch for spinner dolphins and humpback whale sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax aboard the catamaran with a catered lunch, or return to port and visit the charming town of Hanapepe (Kauai's 'Biggest Little Town') for art galleries, local shops, and a stroll across the historic swinging bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed sunset dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure for the catamaran — continental spread, fresh fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Catered gourmet lunch served aboard the catamaran — fresh sandwiches, tropical fruit, local snacks, and open bar with beer, wine, and non-alcoholic beverages.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Plantation House at the Grand Hyatt Kauai or Tidepools Restaurant — a romantic, open-air thatched-roof restaurant set over koi ponds with exceptional seafood and Hawaiian regional cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Napali Coast catamaran through Na Pali Catamaran or Holo Holo Charters for a premium experience. Morning departures offer calmer seas and better wildlife sightings. Apply reef-safe sunscreen and bring a light layer as it can be breezy on the water. The cruise lasts approximately 5–6 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private ATV or horseback riding tour through Kauai's interior — explore the lush valleys, red dirt trails, and panoramic ridgelines of the island's stunning interior landscape. Several ranches near Poipu and Koloa offer guided luxury experiences suitable for families with children of various ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Poipu Beach — consistently ranked one of America's best beaches — for a final family beach afternoon. Snorkel the rocky reef areas for green sea turtles, build sandcastles, and enjoy the calm, protected waters. The resort concierge can arrange premium beach setup with chairs, umbrellas, and a cooler stocked with refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell luau or cultural evening at the resort, followed by a special family dinner to celebrate the penultimate night of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — loco moco, fresh fruit platters, Belgian waffles with lilikoi (passion fruit) syrup, and Kauai-grown coffee.
meals.lunch: Beachside picnic at Poipu Beach arranged by the resort concierge — gourmet sandwiches, fresh poke, tropical fruit, and chilled beverages.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Red Salt at the Koa Kea Hotel (Poipu) — an intimate, award-winning restaurant featuring contemporary Hawaiian cuisine with impeccable ocean views and an exceptional wine and cocktail program.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the ATV or horseback tour operator accepts children and verify minimum age/height requirements. Wear closed-toe shoes for the ATV/horseback activity. The Poipu Beach park area has lifeguards on duty — ideal for families. Book the farewell dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the Maha'ulepu Heritage Trail — a stunning coastal path near Poipu with dramatic sea cliffs, hidden beaches, and incredible views. A peaceful, memorable way to say goodbye to Kauai. Return to the resort for a final luxurious breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Kauai resort with private luxury transfer to Lihue Airport (LIH). Depending on departure time, stop at Koloa Town for last-minute souvenir shopping — local macadamia nut products, Hawaiian sea salt, Kauai coffee, and handcrafted jewelry make perfect premium gifts. Fly home from LIH.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. If a late evening flight, enjoy a final meal at the airport or arrange a VIP airport lounge experience.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final resort breakfast — eggs Benedict with crab cake, smoked salmon platters, fresh tropical fruit, and a celebratory mimosa or fresh-pressed juice.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Koloa or Poipu café before heading to the airport — fresh fish wraps, açaí bowls, or shave ice for one last taste of Hawaii.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or a pre-departure meal at the airport if timing allows. Consider packing premium local snacks — macadamia nuts, chocolate-covered coffee beans, and Kauai cookies — for the journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a late checkout if possible to maximize the final morning. Confirm all luggage weight limits given the likely accumulation of gifts and souvenirs. Ensure all inter-island flight confirmations and the international departure flight are reconfirmed 24 hours before. Consider enrolling in TSA PreCheck or Global Entry for a smoother departure experience.
